turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Um, well, I came in because I keep getting stuck on this... this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek. It really bothers me when I see it in photos, or, you know, under the bright store lights where I work. And even when other people tell me they don't see it, it just... it feels like it's the first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation and distress regarding a perceived slight flaw on their nose and cheek that others report not seeing, feeling that others immediately notice it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself checking mirrors, comparing your skin to others, or trying to cover up that spot multiple times a day?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Um, when I'm on my breaks at work, I usually end up in the bathroom just... checking my face in the mirror. I try to fix my hair around it to sort of hide it better. And I definitely catch myself comparing my skin to the girls who come through my checkout line. Sometimes I get so caught up looking in the mirror that I actually take too long, and... I end up being late getting back to the register.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors related to appearance concerns, including mirror checking, camouflaging with hair, and comparing their skin to others.

turns.doctor_question: When you're worried about how you look, is your main fear that this specific spot makes you look flawed or abnormal, or is it more that you're afraid people will judge or embarrass you in social situations in general, regardless of that spot?
turns.patient_response: Um, I think it's mostly just about that specific spot. I don't really worry about people judging me in general, or, like, just being around people. It's just... I feel like that one area makes my face look abnormal. I guess if I didn't have that uneven patch, I wouldn't really be stressed about talking to customers or anything. So it's definitely just about how that spot looks.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient explicitly confirms that their distress centers on a perceived defect on their face ('uneven patch') that they feel makes their appearance look 'abnormal'.
